name: Crusoe
employees: 'over 1,800 employees across five countries' (Series F release, 17 September 2026); 'more than 300 full-time manufacturing staff in Tulsa'; '15,000 skilled workers across our sites' (contractors)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Crusoe is the archetypal power-first AI data-center developer — builder of the Stargate Abilene flagship (1.2 GW for Oracle/OpenAI, first phase live within a year of groundbreaking) plus a new 900 MW Microsoft campus next door, with '6GW+' of gross contracted capacity and '$140B+' of total contracted value by its own count (September 2026) against a claimed 40+ GW pipeline, and a valuation that ran $2.8B → >$10B → $30.9B post-money within twenty-one months on ~$500M of estimated 2025 revenue: the USD 3.9 billion Series F announced 17 September 2026 (co-led by Atreides, Mubadala Capital and Valor; NVIDIA, GIC, QIA, Founders Fund, TPG among the names) is an 'initial closing' with USD 3.11 billion sold per the Form D. September also brought Google named as the customer of the Armstrong County campus outside Amarillo, a USD 65 million-a-year Thinking Machines Lab inference contract and a multi-year Perplexity deal that carry Crusoe Managed Inference past USD 100 million of contracted ARR, three independent directors (Cloudflare's CFO, Digital Realty's former CEO, Tesla co-founder JB Straubel) — and two reversals: SemiAnalysis's ClusterMAX 3.0 dropped Crusoe Cloud from Gold to Bronze ('Crusoe's clusters are exceptionally unreliable'), and the USD 1.25 billion Boom Supersonic turbine order was abandoned. BACKGROUND: Founded 2018 as a flare-gas bitcoin miner; sold that business to NYDIG (March 2025) to become 'the energy-first AI factory company.' The energy stack is the deepest of any developer: 29 GE Vernova aeroderivative turbines (~1 GW), ~750 MW of Bergen reciprocating engines, 29 Boom Superpower turbines ordered in December 2025 and dropped in September 2026, a reported 4.5 GW Engine No. 1 gas JV, 5 GW of ON.energy medium-voltage battery UPS, 12 GWh of Form Energy iron-air storage, and two nuclear plays (Blue Energy gas-to-nuclear conversion up to 1.5 GW; Aalo microreactors). The counter-narrative is equally concrete: Oracle/OpenAI stopped expanding at Abilene (Microsoft took the orphaned ~700-900 MW), Google managed Crusoe off the 1.8 GW Wyoming project over cost/timeline concerns, and Texas permitting for its gas fleet runs through minor-permit pathways now under press scrutiny.
ecosystemRole: We assess Crusoe as the purest test of whether 'energy-first' development is a durable business or a leveraged construction cycle — and as one of the most instructive buyer accounts in this file for power and storage vendors. Basis: its procurement list reads like this report's supplier index (GE Vernova turbines, Bergen engines, ON.energy MV-BESS at 5 GW — one of the largest battery-UPS commitments anywhere, Form Energy iron-air, Blue Energy and Aalo nuclear), and its build speed (200+ MW energized in under a year at Abilene) is the industry's proof that behind-the-fence generation beats the interconnection queue. The risk side is customer concentration in its most acute form: single-customer decisions reshaped the company twice in 2026 (Oracle/OpenAI halting Abilene expansion; Google ejecting it from Wyoming).

productsAndServices.name: AI-factory campus development (design-build-operate)
productsAndServices.description: The core business: Abilene Campus 1 (1.2 GW, 8 buildings, ~4M sq ft for Oracle/OpenAI — first phase live September 2025, each building sized for up to 50,000 GB200 NVL72s), Abilene Campus 2 (900 MW for Microsoft, two 336 MW-IT-load buildings, first energized mid-2027, bringing the site to 2.1 GW), Childress TX with Lancium (1.0 GW, construction from Q3 2026), plus two unnamed Texas campuses and one Missouri campus under contract, and a reported ~1.6 GW Meta agreement across Childress and Warrenton MO. Financing via JVs (Blue Owl/Primary Digital $15B at Abilene; $7.1B JPMorgan-led construction loan). Armstrong County, Texas (Claude, outside Amarillo): on 28 September 2026 Crusoe named itself 'the developer of Google's data center campus under construction in Armstrong County' — ground broken June 2025, 'more than 5,500 skilled laborers on-site daily', closed-loop non-evaporative liquid cooling; the release states no megawatts, and the Texas filings press reported in July (seven buildings, 'more than 1GW') are not confirmed by the company.
productsAndServices.positioning: The fastest large-scale builder in the sector — DCD's North American Data Center Project of the Year. The merchant-developer model (The Information: ~$30B capex through 2030 with ~$18B expected from selling development stakes) means Crusoe flips assets as much as it operates them.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Anchor-tenant leases (Oracle 15-year at Abilene; Microsoft; Meta reported) via JV-owned buildings.
targetSegments: Hyperscalers and frontier labs needing gigawatt campuses on compressed timelines
productsAndServices.roadmap: Contracted ~4.9 GW; pipeline claimed >40 GW (an 8:1 aspiration ratio); Wyoming (1.8→10 GW ambition) lost to Google's direct management.

productsAndServices.name: Behind-the-fence energy platform (Power Peninsula)
productsAndServices.description: The differentiator: 29 GE Vernova LM2500XPRESS turbines (~1 GW, SCR-equipped, 5-minute start), ~750 MW of Bergen Engines gas reciprocating units (deliveries through 2027, with Piller dynamic stabilization), a reported 4.5 GW Engine No. 1/GE Vernova gas JV, 5 GW of ON.energy 'AI UPS' medium-voltage BESS (commissioning 2026-27, ERCOT ride-through validated), 12 GWh of Form Energy iron-air 100-hour storage (from 2027), solar/wind/grid integration, and nuclear optionality (Blue Energy: gas bridge 2028 → nuclear 2031 at Port of Victoria; Aalo: 10 MWe reactor pilots toward 50 MWe plants by 2029). Dropped from the stack in September 2026: the USD 1.25 billion order for 29 Boom Supersonic Superpower turbines (42 MW each, first deliveries 2027) — Boom's CEO: 'Crusoe and Boom are no longer launching our Superpower turbine together'; Crusoe's spokesman: the energy plans 'haven't changed', it still intends to use turbines, 'just not Boom's' (TechCrunch, 25 September). At Armstrong County the stated power is Serena's adjacent Goodnight 1 (265.5 MW, operating) and Goodnight 2 (265.5 MW, under construction) wind farms, with surplus exported to the grid; a Cleanview-reported permit application for a 933 MW gas plant at the site is press, not company.
productsAndServices.positioning: No other developer publishes an energy stack this deep — it is simultaneously the sector's biggest showcase for bridge-power vendors and its most gas-dependent 'clean' brand (the flare-gas identity was sold with the bitcoin business; carbon capture remains a plan).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Owned/JV generation serving its own campuses; Power Peninsula multi-source integration.
targetSegments: Its own campuses; >20 GW of energy projects claimed in development
productsAndServices.roadmap: The Texas Tribune documented the permitting exposure: Abilene's plant runs on minor 'permit by rule' instruments, with a pending major permit for 41 more turbines that would rank among Texas's largest fossil plants.

productsAndServices.name: Crusoe Cloud & modular (Spark, Edge Zones)
productsAndServices.description: GPU cloud (GB200/B200/H200/H100, AMD MI355X/MI300X; managed Kubernetes/Slurm; customers include Figure AI, Cursor, Together AI, Windsurf; 99.98% uptime cited) plus Crusoe Industries manufacturing (Arvada CO and Tulsa OK factories; Spark modular data centers, power distribution centers, switchgear) and Edge Zones (Spark-based cloud zones deployable in ~three months). The Redwood Materials microgrid (20 MW / second-life EV batteries + solar, 24 Spark units) is the flagship distributed deployment.
productsAndServices.positioning: Sacra frames CoreWeave as the scale neocloud and Crusoe as the energy-differentiated one; cloud bookings grew 5x in the first three quarters of 2025 — but the developer business, not cloud ARR, carries the valuation. SemiAnalysis's ClusterMAX 3.0 (23 September 2026) cut Crusoe Cloud from Gold to Bronze — 'the problems go back to the fundamentals: reliability and hygiene', 'responsible for the majority of this round's hardware failures', 'Crusoe comes in towards the bottom of our Bronze category' — while crediting the Atero acquisition with 'skyrocketing Crusoe to the top of many buyer's lists when it comes to inference endpoint quality'; the company says Managed Inference passed USD 100 million of contracted ARR (Thinking Machines Lab USD 65 million a year; Perplexity multi-year) and NVIDIA granted Exemplar Cloud validation on HGX B300 in Iceland (21 September).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Cloud contracts; modular product sales; sovereign deployments.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Brighton, CO modular factory (~$200M+) targets full operation Q3 2026 — the 'grab-and-go' pivot Forbes profiled.

recentDevelopments.headline: Crusoe names Google: 'today announced it is the developer of Google's data center campus under construction in Armstrong County outside of Amarillo' — ground broken June 2025, 5,500 workers on site, direct connection to Serena's Goodnight 1 (265.5 MW, operating) and Goodnight 2 (265.5 MW, under construction) wind farms, closed-loop cooling; no MW or capex stated
recentDevelopments.read: Google is back as a Crusoe customer three months after managing it off the Wyoming project — on a wind-connected campus, not a gas one.

recentDevelopments.headline: TechCrunch: the USD 1.25 billion order for 29 Boom Supersonic Superpower turbines (first deliveries 2027) is off — Boom's CEO: 'Crusoe and Boom are no longer launching our Superpower turbine together'; Crusoe: energy plans 'haven't changed', it still intends turbines 'just not Boom's'; Boom says it will deliver 'about 250MW of Superpowers next year to other sites'
recentDevelopments.read: The first supplier to fall out of the deepest private-developer energy stack — and the one that was unproven; GE Vernova and Bergen stand.

recentDevelopments.headline: Thinking Machines Lab signs a 'USD 65 million annual agreement' for Crusoe Managed Inference — Inkling and GLM 5.2/5.3 models on a dedicated HGX B200 Tailored Deployment; 'past $100 million in contracted ARR less than a year from launch'
recentDevelopments.read: The inference line is the one Crusoe Cloud product with a disclosed revenue scale, and the one ClusterMAX praised.

recentDevelopments.headline: SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX 3.0 drops Crusoe Cloud from Gold to Bronze: 'in the managed clusters business, TCO comes down to goodput, and goodput comes down to reliability, and Crusoe's clusters are exceptionally unreliable'; the oldest Linux kernel and GPU drivers tested, 'the majority of this round's hardware failures', a 'surprisingly lethargic response'; 'we at one point viewed Crusoe as the #2 neocloud in the world … Oh, how the mighty have fallen'; the Atero inference acquisition praised
recentDevelopments.read: The developer business raised USD 3.9 billion the week the cloud business lost two tiers — the rating lands on the smaller half of the company, but it is the half the valuation narrative calls 'vertically integrated'.

recentDevelopments.headline: Three independent directors: Thomas Seifert (Cloudflare CFO; to chair the Audit Committee), Bill Stein (former Digital Realty CEO; CIO of Primary Digital Infrastructure, Crusoe's Abilene JV partner; Chairman of Verne) and JB Straubel (Redwood Materials founder; Tesla co-founder and former CTO); the board reaches eight
recentDevelopments.read: An audit-committee chair who took Cloudflare public and a data-centre REIT builder — the board of a company 'constantly evaluating' the public market.

recentDevelopments.headline: Series F: 'the initial closing of its anticipated $3.9 billion Series F funding round, at a $30.9 billion post-money valuation', co-led by Atreides, Mubadala Capital and Valor, with Founders Fund, GIC, NVIDIA, QIA, Radical Ventures, TPG and some thirty others; Form D shows USD 3.11 billion of USD 3.90 billion sold; '$140B+' TCV, '6GW+' gross contracted, '1GW+' delivered, 'over 1,800 employees'
recentDevelopments.read: The July talks closed above the reported price; the company's first stated TCV puts it in Nscale's and CoreWeave's bracket on contract value while revenue stays an estimate.

recentDevelopments.headline: Perplexity: multi-year partnership 'across the full model lifecycle' — training on dedicated GB300 NVL72 clusters, serving through Managed Inference; Perplexity Enterprise Pro and Max for Crusoe's 1,800 employees in return; value and capacity undisclosed
recentDevelopments.read: A consumer-scale inference customer on the cloud, named alongside NVIDIA — the kind of logo the Bronze rating says the clusters have trouble keeping.

recentDevelopments.headline: Second Tulsa manufacturing plant opens (400,000 sq ft; about 1 million sq ft of national manufacturing): medium-voltage switchgear, switchboards, enclosures, controls, copper busbar; 'more than 2,500 switchboards supplied to Crusoe's flagship Stargate Project site in Abilene'; 300-plus Tulsa staff
recentDevelopments.read: In-house electrical manufacturing is the part of 'vertically integrated' no rating agency or rater disputes.

recentDevelopments.headline: Oracle Q1 FY2027: at Abilene 'We delivered 131 thousand GPUs there in Q1, 1.9x the volume delivered in Q4' and '6 of the 8 campus buildings, representing 618 megawatts and 75% of total capacity have now been delivered to the customer'; 'The recently released GPT-6 Astra was trained at our site in Abilene'
recentDevelopments.read: The flagship keeps delivering on schedule for the customer that stopped expanding there — the proof point and the ceiling in one sentence.

recentDevelopments.headline: Aalo Atomics partnership targets the first nuclear-powered AI factory — 10 MWe pilot at Idaho National Laboratory in 2027, 50 MWe plants at Crusoe sites by end-2029
recentDevelopments.read: The second nuclear play in nine months; ON.energy's 5 GW AI-UPS deal landed nine days earlier — the energy stack keeps compounding.

recentDevelopments.headline: Childress, TX campus with Lancium — 1.0 GW at full scale, construction from Q3 2026, for an unnamed hyperscaler (Meta per Bloomberg's ~1.6 GW two-site report)
recentDevelopments.read: The Abilene partnership structure (Lancium land/energy, Crusoe design-build-operate) replicated — the model is productizing.

recentDevelopments.read: Against ~$500M estimated 2025 revenue, the discussed valuation is ~60x trailing — the entire mark hinges on a projected 4x revenue jump in 2026 from Stargate/Microsoft execution.

recentDevelopments.read: The sharpest independent counter to the execution story — no signed customer agreement ever existed, and the project continues without Crusoe as Google's Project Tembo.

recentDevelopments.headline: Bergen Engines ~750 MW reciprocating-engine agreement (438 MW firm + 310 MW LOI), deliveries through 2027, with Piller dynamic power stabilization
recentDevelopments.read: Diversifies the generation stack beyond turbines — engines plus flywheel-class stabilization address the GPU transient problem at the generation side.

recentDevelopments.headline: 13 ProEnergy PE6000 gas turbines ordered (650 MW) for hyperscale AI factories, delivery summer 2027 — dual-sourced alongside 29 GE Vernova LM2500XPRESS units
recentDevelopments.read: Refurbished 747-core turbines now bid head-to-head with new OEM iron inside Crusoe's fleet — schedule is the product against 2029-2030 OEM queues.

recentDevelopments.headline: 900 MW Abilene Campus 2 announced for Microsoft — two 336 MW-IT buildings, 900 MW on-site plant plus MV battery storage, first building mid-2027
recentDevelopments.read: The silver lining of the Oracle/OpenAI expansion halt (Bloomberg, March 24): Microsoft leased the orphaned capacity — anchor churn resolved by an even bigger anchor.

recentDevelopments.headline: Form Energy: 12 GWh of iron-air batteries (up to 100-hour duration) from 2027; Redwood Materials microgrid expanded to 20 MW / 24 Spark units
recentDevelopments.read: Long-duration storage enters the AI-campus stack — the 'Bring Your Own Capacity' framing turns multi-day storage into interconnection currency.

recentDevelopments.headline: Series E: $1.375B at >$10B valuation (Valor and Mubadala co-led; NVIDIA, Fidelity, Founders Fund in); power pipeline claimed >45 GW
recentDevelopments.read: The round that repriced the company 3.6x in ten months; an employee tender at ~$13B followed within weeks.

recentDevelopments.headline: Stargate Abilene phase 1 live on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure — first two buildings energized within one year of construction start
recentDevelopments.read: The proof point the whole thesis rests on: gigawatt-class AI capacity delivered at behind-the-fence speed.

recentDevelopments.headline: Bitcoin/flare-gas business sold to NYDIG (~135 employees transferred; lifetime: 2.7M tons GHG mitigated, ~22 Bcf gas kept from flaring)
recentDevelopments.read: The founding identity divested — the climate story now rests on future carbon capture and nuclear, not current operations.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Crusoe's genuine edge is time-to-power execution, demonstrated at scale. Basis: 200+ MW energized at Abilene within a year of groundbreaking, substation energized in under six months, 91-day-class build cadence industry-verified — capabilities no incumbent developer matched publicly in the same window. September 2026 adds to both columns: Oracle reports 618 MW and six of eight Abilene buildings delivered with 131,000 GPUs placed in a quarter, and Google names Crusoe the developer of its Armstrong County campus — while the Boom turbine order, the most speculative item in the energy stack, was dropped.

(High confidence) We assess customer concentration is the defining fragility, proven twice in 2026. Basis: Oracle/OpenAI halted Abilene expansion (financing stalled, needs shifted per Bloomberg) and Google managed Crusoe off Wyoming — in both cases a single counterparty decision removed or reassigned gigawatt-scale work; Microsoft's arrival cured the first but confirmed the dependency structure. The Series F release counters with breadth — '$140B+' TCV, Google back at Armstrong County, Perplexity and Thinking Machines Lab on the cloud — but discloses no customer split, so the concentration cannot be measured from the company's side.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the business is closer to a leveraged merchant developer than a cloud company, and the valuation marks assume otherwise. Basis: The Information's reported ~$30B capex / ~$18B stake-sale-proceeds plan, the ~60x trailing revenue multiple at the discussed $30B round, and Futuriom's 'construction kingpin' framing — cloud bookings grow fast but the economics run through asset flips and JV debt ($7.1B JPMorgan-led at Abilene alone). ClusterMAX 3.0 sharpens the point from the cloud side: the rater that once called Crusoe the second-best neocloud now puts the clusters 'towards the bottom of our Bronze category' for reliability, the week investors priced the whole at USD 30.9 billion — the price is for the developer and the inference line (USD 100 million-plus contracted ARR, the only disclosed cloud revenue scale), not for managed clusters.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the gas-heavy energy stack carries accumulating regulatory and reputational exposure. Basis: minor-permit pathways for the Abilene plant (Texas Tribune), a pending major permit that would rank among Texas's largest fossil plants, community cost-shifting reporting (85%/20-year abatements), and a 'clean' brand whose flare-gas substance was sold to NYDIG — the Form Energy/nuclear deals hedge the narrative but deliver post-2027. The Armstrong County release leads with wind (2 × 265.5 MW, Serena) and says nothing about the 933 MW gas plant whose permit application Cleanview reported — the framing has moved toward renewables and 'across the meter' export even as the Texas gas fleet stands.

(Low confidence) We assess the 40+ GW pipeline converts at well under half. Basis: the 8:1 pipeline-to-contract ratio, the Wyoming loss showing pipeline entries can evaporate pre-contract, and Microsoft's own public oversupply predictions — but conversion evidence is genuinely mixed (Meta's reported 1.6 GW and Childress landed within weeks of the Wyoming exit).

Collection gaps (v7): no audited revenue; the Series F is an initial close (USD 3.11 billion of USD 3.90 billion per the Form D) and total funding to date is not stated anywhere; the Armstrong County campus has no company-stated megawatts, capex or completion date; the Thinking Machines Lab cluster site and the Perplexity deal's value are undisclosed; no Crusoe statement on the ClusterMAX downgrade exists; no replacement turbine supplier has been named since Boom; Bloomberg, CNBC and DCD pages in the window were paywalled or blocked and are cited through reprints.

INDICATORS TO WATCH — *Q4 2026 — the final close of the Series F:* a Form D amendment showing the remaining USD 792 million sold, or a company statement of total funding. *Any replacement for the Boom turbines:* the stack is 29 GE Vernova units and Bergen engines short of the dropped 1.2 GW; a new order names the direction. *Armstrong County:* a company-stated megawatt figure, the fate of the 933 MW gas-plant permit, and Google's first public reference to Crusoe at the site. *Abilene buildings 7 and 8 (the last 25%) and Shackleford:* Oracle's Q2 FY2027 call (December). *ClusterMAX and the cloud:* whether Managed Inference ARR keeps compounding past USD 100 million while the managed-cluster rating sits at Bronze; any public reliability remediation. *An S-1:* bankers were met in September; Lochmiller says a listing 'probably does make sense … at some point'.

The site that proved the whole program buildable.

relationships.note: LM2500XPRESS fleet powers Crusoe sites; GEV turbines anchor the 4.5GW gas JV.
relationships.context: Crusoe runs GEV LM2500XPRESS packaged aeroderivatives (>99.8% availability) as prime power, dual-sourcing 29 XPRESS units alongside ProEnergy's PE6000s, and its 4.5GW gas-generation JV (Engine No. 1/Chevron) is built on GE Vernova turbines.

relationships.note: 13 PE6000s (650 MW) ordered for hyperscale AI factories, delivery summer 2027.
relationships.context: April 2026: Crusoe ordered 13 ProEnergy PE6000 packages (650 MW) — refurbished 747/767-core aeroderivatives bid head-to-head against GEV's LM2500XPRESS inside the same fleet, won on 2027 delivery against OEM queues stretching to 2029-2030.

relationships.note: 5 GW of AI UPS™ deploying across multiple hyperscale campuses, commissioning 2026-2027.
relationships.context: July 2026: Crusoe and ON.energy agreed to deploy 5 GW of medium-voltage, BESS-based AI UPS — ride-through-certified (NOGRR 282), FEOC-clean — across Crusoe campuses. The category-making battery-buffer award of the AIDC buildout, sitting beside Crusoe's gas fleet as the stability layer.

relationships.via: 100-hour iron-air multi-day storage under a bring-your-own-capacity reservation
relationships.note: Crusoe reserved 12 GWh of Form Energy iron-air capacity for its AI data centres, with deliveries starting in 2027.
relationships.context: Announced at CERAWeek on 24 March 2026, with Crusoe securing reserved volume, pricing and delivery terms and all systems to be built at Form Factory 1 in Weirton, West Virginia. It is the only Form agreement publicly described as binding on volume and price, and at 12 GWh it is the second largest in Form's order book after the 30 GWh Google and Xcel project. For this dossier it is the long-duration leg of the deepest energy stack any data-centre developer here has assembled, alongside the GE Vernova turbines, Bergen engines and ON.energy medium-voltage batteries already recorded. The technology is a different product from those: 100-hour discharge at 35–50% round-trip efficiency, cycling roughly eight to thirteen times a year, bought for multi-day firming rather than ride-through.

relationships.note: Letter of intent for Heron Link solid-state transformers reported in June 2025, tied to the Abilene campus; Heron names Crusoe as one of its two disclosed customers.
relationships.context: Bloomberg reported on 3 June 2025 that Heron Power had 'inked preliminary deals with firms including Crusoe', and DCD headlined a letter of intent tied to the Abilene, Texas campus; Latitude Media's August 2026 factory coverage names Crusoe and Intersect Power as the only two customers Heron has disclosed. Crusoe has announced nothing itself, no order size or delivery date is public, and Heron Link is pre-production (mass production slated for late 2027 at Morgan Hill, California). Recorded one-sidedly from Heron's side as an announced engagement; Crusoe's own 800 V DC power path at Abilene is not documented (collection gap).

relationships.note: Crusoe is 'the developer of Google's data center campus under construction in Armstrong County outside of Amarillo' (company release, 28 September 2026) — the second Google engagement after Google managed Crusoe off the Wyoming project in June 2026.
relationships.context: The 28 September 2026 release: 'Crusoe, the AI factory company, today announced it is the developer of Google's data center campus under construction in Armstrong County outside of Amarillo … We broke ground in June 2025 and are building at the same swift pace we set in Abilene.' Power is Serena's Goodnight 1 and 2 wind farms (265.5 MW each) with surplus exported to the grid; the release states no megawatts or capex. Google's side of the record is its Texas Energy Impact Fund support in the county; Google has not named Crusoe. The Energy Mag reports a Cleanview permit application for a 933 MW gas plant at the site and Google telling Cleanview it 'had not signed an agreement to purchase electricity from the gas plant'.

relationships.note: Digital Realty's former CEO Bill Stein (2014–2022; co-founder and CIO 2004–2014) joined Crusoe's board on 17 September 2026 as an independent director; he is CIO of Primary Digital Infrastructure, Crusoe's Abilene joint-venture partner.

relationships.via: Abilene joint venture (with Primary Digital Infrastructure)
relationships.note: Equity co-sponsor, through Blue Owl Real Assets funds, of the USD 15bn joint venture funding Crusoe's 1.2 GW Abilene campus.
relationships.context: Crusoe's 21 May 2025 release: 'Crusoe in combination with funds managed by Blue Owl's Real Assets platform along with Primary Digital Infrastructure will jointly sponsor the construction of six new buildings'. It does not split debt and equity or state Blue Owl's share.

policyExposure.exposure: The Texas Tribune documented that Abilene's on-site plant runs on minor 'permit by rule' instruments now under press scrutiny, with a pending major permit for 41 more turbines that would rank among Texas's largest fossil plants; the dossier assesses the gas-heavy energy stack carries accumulating regulatory and reputational exposure, alongside community cost-shifting reporting (85%/20-year abatements).

metrics.name: Priced rounds
metrics.actual: $2.8B (Series D, Dec 2024) → >$10B (Series E, Oct 2025) → $30.9B post-money (Series F, Sep 2026)
metrics.result: Employee tender ~$13B (Nov 2025); secondary marks ~$23.6B (June 2026); the ~$30B 'in talks' of July 2026 (Bloomberg) landed at $30.9B post-money on a $3.9B round — implied pre-money about $27B (derived, not stated)

metrics.name: Series F (initial closing)
metrics.actual: 'the initial closing of its anticipated $3.9 billion Series F funding round, at a $30.9 billion post-money valuation', co-led by Atreides Management, Mubadala Capital and Valor Equity Partners, with Founders Fund, GIC, NVIDIA, Qatar Investment Authority, Radical Ventures and TPG; Form D (17 September 2026): offering USD 3,901,017,922, USD 3,108,543,889 sold to 108 investors from 31 August, 'include the amount of certain previously issued simple agreements for future equity'; a second Form D records USD 595.9 million of options and warrants sold to 52 investors from 17 July
metrics.result: About USD 792 million of the round remained unsold at filing; no debt was disclosed alongside; SemiAnalysis Capital is listed among the new investors six days before SemiAnalysis's rating downgraded the cloud. Cooley advised

periods.commentary: A ~10x mark-up in twenty months on unaudited financials. The Hustle Fund framing is the fair one: the valuation hinges on Stargate/Microsoft execution converting the 2026 revenue projection.

financials.commentary: Private; no audited public statements. Revenue remains estimate-only (Sacra), while the company now states its own scale in contract value (USD 140 billion-plus TCV), gigawatts (6 GW-plus contracted, 1 GW-plus delivered) and valuation (USD 30.9 billion post-money, Series F). The Form D is the only primary record of the round and shows an initial close, not a completed one.
